title.narrative: Community Action for Peace and Socio Economic Development (CAPSED)

description.narrative: The proposed work aims to address the profound intensity of religious identity in Nigeria, which is recognized as one of the highest globally (Paden, 2008). This intensity is evident in the way Nigerians prioritize their religious affiliations over other aspects of their identity. Surveys indicate that 76% of Christians and 91% of Muslims regard their religion as more significant than their ethnic or national identities. Such a strong emphasis on religious identity has led to notable divisions and conflicts between Christian and Muslim communities, particularly in how these identities influence social interactions and political affiliations. The work seeks to explore how religious identity shapes various aspects of Nigerian culture, including dietary practices, clothing, worldview, political affiliations, and belief systems. This cultural dimension is crucial as it directly affects community dynamics, economic development, and environmental sustainability. By understanding these influences, the initiative can better address the challenges posed by religious differentiation and conflict. A key focus of the proposal is the promotion of Freedom of Religion and Belief (FoRB). It emphasizes the need for effective leadership within cultural and religious institutions. The work also envisions empowering religious leaders and institutions to collaborate towards achieving social harmony. Another critical goal is to prepare these leaders to engage constructively with government bodies and civil society actors. Finally, the proposal aims to reduce vulnerability among marginalized groups, particularly women, children, and youth. Agriculture to enable them be vanguards of religious tolerance and socioeconomic development The project involves strengthening the capacity of 60 traditional and religious leaders including Persons with Disability (PWDs) around Freedom of Religion and Believe and sustainable agriculture.
